transcript:
This message comes from Capital One with the Venture X Card.
Earn unlimited double miles and a $300 annual Capital One travel credit.
Capital One.
What's in your wallet?
Terms of fly.
Details at CapitalOne.com.
This is NPR News Now.
The latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Janine Herbst.
Millions of people are bracing for delays at airports and highways across the country
today as powerful storms threaten to disrupt holiday travel.
Strong winds expected in New York City led officials there to postpone the annual Macy's
Thanksgiving Day parade, as NPR's Kat Lonsdorf reports.
Almost every part of the country has some kind of weather concern.
Ongoing extreme high tides on the West Coast, snow expected in parts of the Midwest, and
in the South and Southeast, a major storm is making its way up the coast.
Officials in many states along the East Coast are warning people to stay home throughout
the day as that storm barrels through.
For the first time in its 100-year history, the Macy's Thanksgiving Day parade has been
postponed, as high winds are expected in New York City up to 60 miles per hour.
Organizers had already begun inflating the iconic giant balloons when officials made
the call to move the spectacle to Saturday for safety reasons.
The East Coast storm is expected to clear by the weekend.
Kat Lonsdorf, NPR News, Washington.
In Northern California, several coastal communities faced evacuation orders yesterday as floodwaters
inundated homes and streets.
Theo Greenlee from Jefferson Public Radio has more.
Residents of the small waterfront community of King Salmon were ordered to evacuate Tuesday
as rising water flooded local streets.
But a day later, Eli Blassingame was still in his trailer at a local RV park where he's
lived for three years, even as floodwaters rose.
"It went probably up to my thigh, the water did, so I had to start putting on hip waders
because the tide was coming in."
The National Weather Service says unusually high tides, El Nino, and strong southerly
winds have pushed water levels near historic highs.
Forecasters say flooding remains possible through Friday.
For NPR News, I'm Theo Greenlee in Beaverton.
With questions swirling about the reinstatement of NVIDIA CEO Jensen Huang, NPR's Andrea
Hsu reports critics say the board failed in its duties.
Corporate boards exist to make informed and deliberate decisions that are in the best
interest of the company and its shareholders.
Tulane Business Professor Rob Laca says that didn't happen at NVIDIA.
He describes the board's decision to reinstate Huang as rash and focused on short-term profits.
He says that does not make for a robust economy.
"Everyone who's leading these AI companies are telling us that they want to do what is
in the best long-term interest of humanity.
This to me speaks to quite the opposite."
In a statement announcing Huang's return, NVIDIA board chair Harvey Jones said the board
believes Huang is the right person to lead NVIDIA, and that his reinstatement is in the
best interests of the company's stockholders, employees, partners, and customers.
Andrea Hsu, NPR News.
Wall Street is closed today in observance of the Thanksgiving holiday.
You're listening to NPR News.
The former Army psychiatrist who killed 13 people and injured 32 others in the 2009 mass
shooting at Fort Hood is seeking to postpone his execution.
A federal judge has scheduled a public hearing on Nidal Hassan's request for a stay for
this coming Monday, just three days before the planned execution.
Texas Public Radio's Eleanor Fitzgerald has more.
Kerry Cahill is the daughter of Michael Cahill, the lone civilian killed in the attack.
For her, Hassan's plea for time to argue against perceived wrongdoings in his case is opening
up old wounds.
"Giving him the death penalty makes him a martyr.
Hegseff is giving him what he wants.
He gets to go down in a hail of bullets in front of everybody.
And he might be scared now because it's suddenly coming up.
But when he went in that day, he didn't think he was walking out."
Kerry and her sister Kaylee said they hope the general public can focus on remembering
their dad and the victims and not giving attention to Hassan.
I'm Eleanor Fitzgerald in San Antonio.
The federal judge has agreed to block the FCC from conducting an early review of local
TV broadcast licenses held by ABC and its parent company, Disney.
The network accuses the FCC of violating its free speech rights in retaliation against
programming decisions the Trump administration dislikes.
U.S. District Judge Lauren Olicon granted Disney a temporary restraining order and a preliminary
injunction on First Amendment grounds.
I'm Janine Herbst, and you're listening to NPR News from Washington.
This message comes from Rosetta Stone, offering an alternative approach to language learning.
Without relying on traditional memorization, the platform guides users to intuitively think
in a second language.
More information at RosettaStone.com.

topics.text: Millions face holiday travel delays as powerful storms threaten airports and highways nationwide
Macy's Thanksgiving Day parade postponed to Saturday over high winds forecast for New York City
Northern California coastal communities ordered to evacuate as floodwaters inundate homes, streets
NVIDIA board's reinstatement of CEO Jensen Huang draws criticism from business professor Rob Laca
Former Army psychiatrist Nidal Hassan seeks stay of execution for 2009 Fort Hood shooting
Judge blocks FCC early review of ABC and Disney local TV broadcast licenses over free speech concerns
